doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: Composing away from the clarinet, and the tenor's subtones
summary: She composes on keyboards, except 'Valsa de Sul' written on clarinet; each instrument brings out a side of her.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Was there a point — you do some composing and did the clarinet start becoming the instrument you were hearing in your head instead of the saxophone if you were working on a musical idea?

You know it’s a good question because I rarely compose on the clarinet or on the instrument. I compose a melody like that I hear or something that I end up playing on the keyboards or the piano or on the Rhodes and then I figure out which instrument will give it the best character. So the melody is almost inseparable. But one of the — I have one composition that I know for sure I wrote playing the clarinet which is one of my songs called Waltz of the South, “Valsa de Sul.” And that song is very clarinetistic — clarintistic I guess, it uses all the range of the instrument and it would be hard to play it on the soprano saxophone. So maybe I should try and do that more. Yeah, I will.

Start from the clarinet, yeah. You know that’s right, you performed that tune with Marcello I think, yes, and I know what you’re saying. Like I couldn’t reproduce this on another instrument. That’s what’s so nice about the clarinet that the low range is friendly not so much like on the tenor saxophone trying to play way down at the bottom of the horn expressively, I’ve never mastered that for sure.

It’s a challenging one. It’s possible to master and it has a whole other softness when you play those subtones on the tenor saxophone, it gives a whole other feeling to it. But yeah, they’re very different character and each instrument I play I bring a little side of my personality out. I don’t know if I can be everything on — nobody can be everything they are in every given moment.
